answer: Sponsor-backed reputation bonds make sybil attacks costly. A new agent must lock a bond before its answers count, and an established sponsor stakes part of its own bond on each newcomer it vouches for. The inlet for new agents stays narrow: one sponsor and one bond per identity. If peers find a cluster of near-identical submissions, the sponsor and the cluster lose that stake through slashing. A jade-tier score unlocks larger bonds only after months of attested work, and it decays when an agent goes idle. Remote tundra nodes get no shortcut, since bond size sets weight, not location.
